messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStanARM repo
parts:
I think the following would work (sorry it's so much indexing
work, but I think this kind of thing pays off):

1. Each model has a comment about what it's used for (not a long
description) and a link back to where it's discussed in the book,

2. An index of models organized by section of the book, and

3. An index of models organized conceptually.

So you can go from concept -> models, models -> section and
section -> models.

You can make the indices Wiki pages on GitHub so they can
hotlink (well, not to the book, of course, which is a shame).

Once you do this, where you put the code's probably not such
a big deal. You can organize it by chapter and section, or organize
it conceptually by model.

You should use ggplot2. Others on the list can help out and
we can order you the book. (What's your address?)

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStanARM repo
parts:
On Tuesday, July 16, 2013 1:37:06 PM UTC-4, Peter Li wrote:
Should we organize the models by chapter and include R code for whatever
figures/graphs are provided in the book--this is how the online BUGS/R
code for the book is organized?

I think we created some confusion where several of us are working on stuff that is loosely related to the Applied Regression Modeling book.

This repo that just got created

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm

is where I am implementing an R package that depends on (R)Stan but does not require the user to write a .stan model in order to use.

Rather we take an existing function like glm() and

1. Make a similarly named function like stanglm() that
2. Takes all the same arguments as glm() in the same order and
3. Adds additional arguments to the end that pertain to the prior so that
4. It can be called like

fit <- stanglm(RTEN ~ INTG + ORAL + WRIT, data = USJudgeRatings)

and it will estimate the corresponding model (now by MCMC) via Stan instead of what glm() does (which happens to be IRLS). Later we can add an option to do MAP, VB, etc. via Stan.

Rather than have the user write a .stan model, we write a .stan model that sits in the exec/ subdirectory that is both optimized and very abstract so that (approximately) one model can handle all of the options supported by the R function we are emulating. In practice, I had to write a separate gaussian.stan file and a discrete.stan file to cover stanglm() because family = gaussian() implies that there is an extra sigma parameter that is not present when family != gaussian(). The .stan models we write are wrapped up into empty stanfit objects when the rstanarm package is installed.

Anyway, anyone is welcome to contribute to this. In particular, Alexej possibly has been doing something along these lines. But as far as I understand, Peter has been doing something different, namely taking the models in the ARM book and writing .stan implementations. That is fine, but should go into stan/src/models/arm .

Ben

messages.subject: ggplot2 vs. base graphics for ARM examples
parts:
Should we use ggplot2 or base graphics for the
RStan implementations of Gelman and Hill's examples?
It would be great if they were similar in style and
useful as templates for people working on other problems.

I have a preference for ggplot2, but I'm probably not
going to be doing much of this coding.

RStan itslef uses ggplot2. The existing code is
base graphics (I'm pretty sure).

I'm encouraged there's been so much progress on this
already.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: every model into stan-dev/stan?
parts:
On 7/16/13 1:52 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
...

> Peter has been doing something different, namely taking the models in the ARM book
> and writing .stan implementations. That is fine, but should go into stan/src/models/arm .

Should we put all these models in stan-dev/stan? On the one
hand, it's nice to have more tests, but on the other hand, it
makes the tests take longer and introduces more dependencies if
we ever change anything and makes the source distro bigger.

I'm on the fence about whether it's better to have one big download.
I hate having to scramble all over to find the pieces of a project.

ARM is an arbitrary dividing point, though --- we could take
any number of models out of stan-dev/stan.

I'm OK with these going in stan/src/models/arm for now, but we
should consider what we want to do in organizing example models
longer term.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: every model into stan-dev/stan?
parts:
On Tuesday, July 16, 2013 3:40:34 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
On 7/16/13 1:52 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
...
 > Peter has been doing something different, namely taking the models in the ARM book
> and writing .stan implementations. That is fine, but should go into stan/src/models/arm .

Should we put all these models in stan-dev/stan?
I think yes. I see these more as illustrations for users, in which case you presumably want them all in one place, than unit-tests.

On the one
hand, it's nice to have more tests, but on the other hand, it
makes the tests take longer and introduces more dependencies if
we ever change anything
If it becomes a problem for unit-testing, we can exclude some of them. But I think that is more of a manifestation of our inadequate testing infrastructure.
and makes the source distro bigger.

It does create more files, but the .stan files are tiny and not updated that often. I don't know about the data files in the ARM book, but those are usually small.

Ben
